sections.overview: This widespread Eurasian ground beetle is a member of Carabus, a genus of large, mostly flightless predatory beetles.
sections.identification: Adults are about 17–32 mm long, with a metallic coppery body and elytra marked by raised longitudinal ridges and broken chain-like rows.
sections.habitat: It occupies fields, meadows, gardens and open woodland, from lowlands into foothills, and often shelters beneath stones or vegetation.
sections.diet: Adults and larvae hunt insects, snails and earthworms, and may also feed on carrion.
sections.behavior: It is active by day and night and runs rapidly across the ground rather than flying.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs in soil; larvae develop as predators, pupate underground and new-generation adults emerge later in the year.
sections.ecology: It belongs to the diverse Carabus ground-beetle genus; similar European species include C. granulatus and C. nemoralis, which differ in elytral sculpture and typical habitat.
sections.conservation: Its German national Red List category is Near Threatened, with strong long-term decline reported; this regional status should not be confused with a global assessment.
